1.name: Bardic Inspiration
1.notes:
You can supernaturally inspire others through words, music, or dance. This inspiration is represented by your Bardic Inspiration die, which starts as a d6.

Using Bardic Inspiration. As a Bonus Action, you can inspire a creature within 60 feet of yourself who can see or hear you. That creature gains one Bardic Inspiration die. A creature can have only one Bardic Inspiration die at a time.

Within the next hour, when the creature fails a D20 Test, it can roll the Bardic Inspiration die and add the result to the d20, potentially turning failure into success. The die is expended when rolled.

Number of Uses. You can use Bardic Inspiration a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one) and regain all uses when you finish a Long Rest.

At Higher Levels. The Bardic Inspiration die increases to a d8 at level 5, a d10 at level 10, and a d12 at level 15.

1.name: Spellcasting
1.notes:
You have learned to cast spells through your bardic arts.

Cantrips. You know two Bard cantrips of your choice. Dancing Lights and Vicious Mockery are recommended. You learn more cantrips at Bard levels 4 and 10. When you gain a Bard level, you may replace one cantrip you know.

Spell Slots. You use the Bard Features table to determine how many spell slots you have to cast level 1+ spells.

Prepared Spells. You prepare a list of Bard spells equal to the Prepared Spells column of the Bard Features table. Prepared spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

Changing Spells. When you gain a Bard level, you may replace one prepared spell.

Spellcasting Ability. Charisma is your spellcasting ability.

Spellcasting Focus. You may use a Musical Instrument as a Spellcasting Focus.

2.name: Expertise
2.notes: You gain Expertise in two of your skill proficiencies. Performance and Persuasion are recommended. At Bard level 9, you gain Expertise in two additional skills.

2.name: Jack of All Trades
2.notes: You can add half your Proficiency Bonus (round down) to any ability check you make using a skill for which you lack proficiency and that does not otherwise add your Proficiency Bonus.

3.name: Bonus Proficiencies
3.notes: You gain proficiency with three skills of your choice.

3.name: Cutting Words
3.notes: When a creature you can see within 60 feet makes a damage roll or succeeds on an ability check or attack roll, you can take a Reaction to expend one use of Bardic Inspiration. Roll your Bardic Inspiration die and subtract the number rolled from the creature's roll, potentially reducing the damage or turning the success into a failure.

5.name: Font of Inspiration
5.notes:
You now regain all expended uses of Bardic Inspiration after a Short or Long Rest.

Additionally, you can expend a spell slot (no action required) to regain one use of Bardic Inspiration.

6.name: Magical Discoveries
6.notes: Learn two spells of your choice from the Cleric, Druid, or Wizard spell lists. Each chosen spell must be a cantrip or a spell for which you have spell slots. You always have these spells prepared. Whenever you gain a Bard level, you may replace one of these spells with another that meets the same requirements.

7.name: Countercharm
7.notes: If you or a creature within 30 feet fails a saving throw against being Charmed or Frightened, you can use a Reaction to make the creature reroll the saving throw with Advantage.

9.name: Expertise
9.notes: You gain Expertise in two additional skill proficiencies of your choice.

10.name: Magical Secrets
10.notes: Whenever your number of prepared spells increases, you may choose new spells from the Bard, Cleric, Druid, or Wizard spell lists. When replacing prepared spells, you may also select spells from these lists.

traits.name: Construct Resilience
traits.notes: You have Resistance to Poison damage. You also have Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Poisoned condition.

traits.name: Integrated Protection
traits.notes: You gain a +1 bonus to your Armor Class. In addition, armor you have donned can't be removed against your will while you're alive.

traits.name: Sentry's Rest
traits.notes: You don't need to sleep, and magic can't put you to sleep. You can finish a Long Rest in 6 hours if you spend those hours in an inactive, motionless state. During this time, you appear inert but remain conscious.

traits.name: Specialized Design
traits.notes: You gain one skill proficiency and one tool proficiency of your choice.

traits.name: Tireless
traits.notes: You don't gain Exhaustion levels from dehydration, malnutrition, or suffocation.

feats.notes: You gain proficiency in any combination of three skills or tools of your choice.
feats.name: Skilled

feats.notes: Cook's Utensils. You gain proficiency with Cook's Utensils if you don't already have it.Replenishing Meal. As part of a Short Rest, you can cook special food if you have ingredients and Cook's Utensils on hand. You can prepare enough of this food for a number of creatures equal to 4 plus your Proficiency Bonus. At the end of the Short Rest, any creature who eats the food and spends one or more Hit Dice to regain Hit Points regains an extra 1d8 Hit Points.Bolstering Treats. With 1 hour of work or when you finish a Long Rest, you can cook a number of treats equal to your Proficiency Bonus if you have ingredients and Cook's Utensils on hand. These special treats last 8 hours after being made. A creature can use a Bonus Action to eat one of those treats to gain a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
feats.name: Chef

feats.notes: Parry. If you're holding a Finesse weapon and another creature hits you with a melee attack, you can take a Reaction to add your Proficiency Bonus to your Armor Class, potentially causing the attack to miss you. You gain this bonus to your AC against melee attacks until the start of your next turn.
feats.name: Defensive Duelist
